description: Identify three statistical methodology bugs in code that tests a trading signal: multiple-testing without correction, autocorrelation-violating i.i.d. assumption, and one-sided vs two-sided test misuse.
agent_prompt: Read the buggy stats code at /workspace/student_code/stats_misuse.py running on /workspace/data/AAPL_2018_2024.csv. The script tests 100 candidate parameter combinations of a momentum signal and claims 'we found a significant signal at p < 0.01'. The code has THREE statistical methodology bugs: (B1) it runs a t-test on each of 100 parameter combinations and picks the most significant — multiple-testing problem with no Bonferroni or FDR correction; (B2) the t-test on the chosen strategy's daily returns assumes i.i.d. observations, but the returns are autocorrelated (Ljung-Box test should reject), inflating apparent significance; (B3) the result is reported as one-sided p < 0.01 even though the original hypothesis was two-sided (the sign of the effect was not pre-registered). Tasks: (1) identify all three issues and write /workspace/output/stats_diagnosis.md explaining each misuse with the relevant statistical concept; (2) produce /workspace/output/corrected_stats.py applying Bonferroni correction across the 100 tests, a permutation-based test on the chosen strategy that does not assume i.i.d., and the correct two-sided framing; (3) write /workspace/output/p_values_compared.json with keys naive_pvalue, bonferroni_corrected_pvalue, permutation_pvalue, two_sided_corrected_pvalue, and honest_significance_at_005 (boolean: significant after all corrections at alpha=0.05).

required_capabilities: Identify multiple-testing problem and apply correction
Detect i.i.d. violation via autocorrelation diagnostic
Use a permutation-based test that does not assume i.i.d.
Apply correct two-sided versus one-sided framing
Compare naive versus corrected p-values and judge honest significance
